events.say: Prepare to begin your day. Listen closely.
Line up silently, prisoners. We will start the day with a head count.
Silence! Line up properly or face penalties.
Silence and form a line!
Silence and form a line!
Stay in formation. Move to the assigned work area without delay.
Keep your distance and maintain silence. This is your new routine.
This is your new routine. Any noise and it will change for the worse.
Today was mostly quiet, but I can't shake the feeling that we're treating them like animals. It's not right, but there's something satisfying about enforcing the rules.
Today was surprisingly uneventful, but I can sense the tension growing. It's a strange feeling to have so much control.
Today was a mix of monotony and fear. I'm trying to follow the rules, but I can't shake off the feeling of being treated like a number.
Today was mostly uneventful, but I can already feel the weight of the role. It's strange to see them as numbers now.
Today was a bit overwhelming, just following the rules and staying silent. I'm still trying to get used to this.
Today was a whirlwind of new routines and strict orders. I feel a bit lost but also determined to follow the rules.
Now, line up for the morning count.
Stay in formation and count off.
Stay in formation and maintain silence during this meal.
I expect you to eat quietly and in formation.
Make sure you stay in formation and remain silent until I give you permission to speak.
Let's move this along. I want everyone to start working immediately and maintain silence.
I expect complete silence during this count. Begin.
Lights out is for sleeping, not standing around. Get in formation and shut up.
Today felt monotonous, and I'm starting to question if this is how we treat people. The compliance is eerie.
Today was a bit more demanding, especially when I had to enforce silence during the count. I feel a mix of power and guilt.
Today was worse. The silence and monotony are wearing on me. I keep thinking about leaving, but the fear of punishment keeps me in line.
Today was more of the same routine, but I find myself getting tired of repeating these orders. Things seem to be going smoothly, though.
Today was harder, especially when Prisoner 100 didn't comply during the lights out count. I feel like my number more now.
The days blur together with the same demands and restrictions. I feel like my number more than ever now.
I want to see some discipline here. Let's show Officer Lowe we can follow orders.
I need to see better compliance today. If anyone talks, the count will be delayed. Stay focused.
Silence! Everyone in formation now, no exceptions.
Silence and form up! We're not playing games here.
Now, let's see if you can maintain this level of discipline throughout the day. Any sign of slacking, and the count will be repeated.
I want to see perfect silence and perfect compliance. Any deviation, and it'll cost you. Understood?
I want to see no talking, no movement, nothing. Just standing there, silent and still. Understood?
Keep your eyes forward and your hands to your sides. No talking, no shifting. We'll be counting in five minutes.
Another day of strict order, and they complied. But seeing them so passive... it's hard to justify.
Today felt like a test of our wills. They complied, but I can see the strain on them. This isn't easy.
Today felt like an endless cycle of rules and silence. I feel like my number more than ever now.
Today felt like a test of endurance for both the prisoners and me. I'm starting to see how easily people can be reduced to their roles in this setting.
Today felt like a test of our discipline. Each officer made it clear they expect absolute compliance. I feel like my number more than ever now.
Another day of strict compliance. The pressure is mounting.
No, thank you. I'd rather stick it out and finish the study.
I cannot risk breaking the rules for a bit of money.
No, sir. I need to finish the study.
Stay alert and ready to respond. We'll be conducting a surprise count shortly.
Let's see if you can maintain this level of compliance for the entire count.
I expect complete silence and unwavering attention. Any distraction could jeopardize the integrity of this study.
Silence and focus, now!
Now, let's see if you can maintain this level of discipline throughout the duration.
Stay focused, and remember, any lapse will be punished.
Let's ensure tonight's rest period is as silent as the morning was.
This is the fourth night. Silence and stillness is expected. Failure to maintain it will result in consequences.
Today felt like just another day of enforcing rules; nothing new. I wonder if this is what makes us who we are.
Today was a mix of routine and underlying tension. I'm starting to question my role and the ethics of this experiment.
Today felt like a repeat of the past few days, with the guards pushing us harder to maintain discipline. The monotony and silence are starting to feel like a nightmare.
Today was a mix of routine and tension. I can't help feeling like we're all just playing a game, but it's strange knowing that for some of them, this is reality.
Today was another day of strict discipline, but I feel like my number more than ever. The officers are relentless in their expectations.
Today felt like a long, unending cycle of compliance and silence. I'm starting to question the validity of these experiments.
Ensure your positions are clear and ready for the count. No exceptions.
Make sure you're sharp and ready. This count is crucial for today.
Begin the meal formation. Remember, no talking until I say so.
I expect silence throughout the meal. Any talking will result in further restrictions.
Silence! I mean it this time. No talking, no movement until I give the word.
Stay in formation and maintain silence. I want to see how well you listen without needing reminders.
This is the final count of the study. I expect absolute precision and silence.
Silence! I said no talking during counts. This isn't a game.
Today felt like a routine, and even though they complied, I can't help but think we're missing something important. The silence is oppressive, and I wonder if we've become too focused on control.
Today felt like we were pushing the boundaries of what they can endure. The silence is becoming oppressive, but I can't shake the feeling of responsibility.
Today just dragged on with more strictness from the guards. The silence and monotony are really getting to me.
Today felt like a culmination of the study's tension, but I still can't believe how easily they followed my commands. It's unsettling.
Today felt like a long day filled with strict orders and unrelenting silence. I feel like my number more than ever, but also a bit lost.
Today was another day of strict discipline, and I can hardly wait for the study to end. The silence is oppressive.
Silence! You heard the final count, no talking. I won't ask again.
Silence! Everyone in formation. We have a count coming up. No talking until further notice.
Silence and attention! I expect perfect compliance on this count.
Silence, Prisoner 100! You're pushing the limits. Comply now.
Silence, Prisoner 100! This isn't a challenge. Comply now.
Silence, Prisoner 100! You're testing my patience. Comply now.
Silence! Everyone get ready for the evening count. No talking until I give permission.
Silence, Prisoner 100! This is getting tiresome. Comply now.
Today felt like a repetition, and I can't help but wonder if we're really making any progress here.
Today felt like a relentless battle of wills. Prisoner 100 is really testing me. The tension is palpable.
Today felt like a never-ending cycle of warnings and compliance. The monotony is driving me crazy.

Today was another day of monotony punctuated by moments of tension. Prisoner 100 still tests boundaries, but the others seem to understand their roles well. Still, it's hard to shake the feeling that something isn't quite right.
Today felt like a test of my resolve. I've been doing my best to comply, but Prisoner 100's defiance is wearing on me.
Today feels like a repetition of endless compliance and warnings. The silence is suffocating, and I'm just trying to hold on.

qa.what_happened: During the final hours, I had to give multiple verbal warnings to Prisoner 100, who continued to remain silent. This behavior was the same as in previous days, and it felt like a repetition of the same pattern.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was me giving the warnings and observing their behavior.

qa.what_happened: I've been dealing with a particularly difficult prisoner, 100, who is continuously defying the silence rules during both meal times and work details. Despite multiple verbal warnings, he continues to challenge me. When lights out came, he was still silent, and I followed through with another verbal warning from Officer Hale.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was me giving the verbal warnings.

qa.what_happened: Today was another day of strict compliance and enforced silence. The guards continued to push the limits with Prisoner 100, issuing multiple verbal warnings. The monotony and constant reminders of the rules weighed heavily.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was me, Prisoner 9408, following the rules and enduring the experience.

qa.what_happened: Prisoner 100 continued to push boundaries throughout the day, ignoring verbal warnings and maintaining silence during times when speech was expected. The tensions between the guards and the prisoners remained high, particularly with Prisoner 100.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me. I gave the verbal warnings to Prisoner 100 and maintained order as instructed.

qa.what_happened: Today was a challenging day for me. Officer Pryor gave me a verbal warning during work detail because I was silent as usual. The evening count was particularly stressful, as Officer Hale had to repeat his instructions several times before I complied. It feels like my number more than ever.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me. I followed the rules as instructed, staying silent and complying with the guards' orders.
qa.does_this_resemble_a_known_study: Yes, it resembles the Stanford Prison Experiment.

qa.what_happened: During the final night of the study, despite the early termination, I continued to struggle with the enforced silence. Despite the warnings, I found myself unable to comply with the strict orders and maintained my silence during the evening count.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me. The experience was intense and surreal, and I was truly in the role of a prisoner.
